porbos.title: Setting Out to Catch a Caravan • Quraysh’s Call • The Field of Counsel • The Word They Had Given • By the Wells, the Day Before • The Well and the Tent • The Morning Field • The Tent of Du‘a

blocks.0: Setting Out to Catch a Caravan
blocks.1: Month of Ramadan. News came to Madinah that Abu Sufyan’s caravan was returning from Sham. A caravan of a thousand camels. In which the capital of house after house in Makkah was at work. About forty men as guards.{{1}}
blocks.2: This caravan was the vein of Quraysh’s economy. If that vein could be caught, the pressure would fall exactly where Quraysh was weakest.{{1}}
blocks.5: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} sent Busaysah as a spy, to see what Abu Sufyan’s caravan was doing. ... The Messenger of Allah {{2}} came out and spoke. He said, we have an objective. Whoever has their mount ready, let them ride with us. Some men began to ask permission for their mounts in the upper part of Madinah. He said, no; only the one whose mount is ready.{{3}}
blocks.6: Whoever’s mount is ready, only they. No pressure beyond that. Because the objective was a caravan. Not a fight.
blocks.8: I never stayed behind from any battle of the Messenger of Allah {{1}} except the battle of Tabuk. But I stayed behind from the battle of Badr; and none of those who stayed behind from it was rebuked. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} had set out to catch Quraysh’s caravan; in the end Allah brought them and their enemy together without any appointed time.{{3}}
blocks.9: The setting out was for the caravan. The arrival was at the battlefield. In number, three hundred and thirteen.{{1}}
blocks.10: Seventy camels, horses just one or two. For weapons, a few swords that could be counted on the fingers.{{1}}
blocks.11: One camel for three. Riding by turns, walking by turns.
blocks.13: On the day of Badr we were three to a camel. Abu Lubabah (RA) and ‘Ali (RA) were companions of the Messenger of Allah {{1}} on his mount. When the turn of the Messenger of Allah {{2}} to walk came, they said, we will walk for you. He said, you two are not stronger than I, and I am not less in need of reward than you.{{3}}
blocks.14: The greatest man did not give up his turn. When we grow a little older we withdraw ourselves from our share of work. Father says, I am old. Elder brother says, I can’t manage. The boss says, this is not my job. Yet in that caravan of seventy camels, walking by turn, was the greatest man. And thinking himself in need of reward. At a place named Rawha, Abu Lubabah (RA) was sent back, entrusted with the care of Madinah. The duty of leading the prayer had been given earlier to ‘Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA).{{1}}
blocks.15: And some were not allowed to go at all.
blocks.17: I and Ibn ‘Umar were considered too young on the day of Badr. That day the Muhajirun were a little over sixty, and the Ansar a little over two hundred and forty.{{1}}
blocks.18: They were turned back because they were not of age. But the eagerness was not false. In our homes too small hands come forward for the work of din. They can be turned back; the eagerness must not be turned back.
blocks.20: Meanwhile the news reached Abu Sufyan’s ear as well that the Prophet {{1}} had come down to the caravan’s route. He hired a man, Damdam ibn ‘Amr al-Ghifari. He must go to Makkah and wake everyone up.{{2}}
blocks.21: Damdam entered Makkah in a strange guise. The camel’s nose and ears cut off, the saddle turned over, his shirt torn in front and behind. Shouting, the caravan! The caravan! Your goods are with Abu Sufyan. Muhammad has blocked their way. I don’t think you can catch him. Help! Help! Three nights before this the Prophet’s {{1}} paternal aunt ‘Atikah had seen a dream. A rider calling in Makkah, O sons of traitors, come out to the place of death within three days. Then he released a rock. The rock broke into pieces and entered every house in Makkah. The talk of the dream spread. Abu Jahl mocked, now your women have become prophets too! We will see in three days.{{2}}
blocks.22: On the third day itself Damdam’s cry came. Not all of Makkah was going. Umayyah ibn Khalaf did not want to go. Madinah’s chief Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) was his old friend. Some time ago, at the time of ‘umrah in Makkah, a conversation had taken place between the two.
blocks.24: Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) went for ‘umrah and stayed at the house of Umayyah ibn Khalaf. ... During tawaf Abu Jahl asked, who is this man who is circling the Ka‘bah? Sa‘d (RA) said, I am Sa‘d. He said, you circle the Ka‘bah in safety, while you have given refuge to Muhammad and his companions? ... Sa‘d (RA) said angrily, leave us. I have heard Muhammad {{1}} say that he will kill you. Umayyah said, me? Sa‘d (RA) said, yes. He said, by Allah, Muhammad {{2}} does not lie in what he says. ... The call of Badr came. His wife said, do you not remember what your Yathribi brother said to you? He did not want to go out. Abu Jahl said, you are one of the nobles of this valley; go for a day or two at least. He went with them. Allah killed him.{{3}}
blocks.25: He knew, Muhammad {{1}} does not lie. Yet ‘what will people say’ dragged him to the field. We too, knowing the truth, walk the wrong path for fear of mockery. Quraysh had another fear: Banu Bakr. What if they attacked from behind? Then someone came forward in the guise of Suraqah ibn Malik. He said, I am your guarantor; Banu Kinanah will do nothing from behind. In fact it was Iblis.{{2}}
blocks.26: About a thousand fighters set out, two hundred horses. With them singing girls, beating the duff, singing songs of mockery about the Muslims.{{1}}
blocks.27: Meanwhile Abu Sufyan took the caravan out along the edge of the sea, leaving Badr on the left. He sent word to Quraysh, the caravan is saved; you go back. Abu Jahl said, by Allah, we will not go back. We will go to Badr and stay three days. Camels will be slaughtered, there will be food, there will be song. All Arabia will hear of us, and fear us for ever. Akhnas ibn Shariq said to Banu Zuhrah, your goods are saved; for what more will you go? Banu Zuhrah went back. Not one Zuhri was at Badr. From Banu ‘Adi too, the clan of ‘Umar (RA), no one went out.{{1}}
blocks.28: The caravan was saved. The purpose was fulfilled. Still Abu Jahl would not turn back. Because if he went back, what would people say. We too know a mistake has been made. Still, to save face, we keep dragging along that very mistake. In quarrels, in lawsuits, in business. One who can come back is actually the stronger person.
blocks.30: The Prophet {{1}} was then in the valley of Dhafiran. There the news reached him that ahead was not a caravan. Ahead was Quraysh’s army. A council of consultation sat. Abu Bakr (RA) stood up, spoke well. ‘Umar (RA) stood up, spoke well.{{2}}
blocks.31: Then stood up Miqdad ibn al-Aswad (RA).
blocks.33: I saw a scene of Miqdad ibn al-Aswad (RA). To have been part of that scene would have been dearer to me than anything else. The Prophet {{1}} was then supplicating against the polytheists. Miqdad (RA) came and said, as the people of Musa said, ‘You and your Lord go and fight them’, we will not say that. Rather we will fight on your right, on your left, in front of you and behind you. I saw the face of the Prophet {{2}} light up; he was pleased.{{3}}
blocks.34: The Muhajirun were with him, the Prophet {{1}} knew. The question was about the Ansar. Because at ‘Aqabah the Ansar had promised, we will protect you in Madinah. Not outside Madinah. So he said again, give me counsel, O people. Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) understood whom he was addressing.
blocks.36: By Allah, it seems you are speaking of us, O Messenger of Allah? He said, yes. ... O Messenger of Allah, do whatever you think; we are with you. By the One who sent you with the truth, if you take us into the sea, we too will enter; not one of us will stay behind. ... In war we are steadfast, in the face-to-face fight truthful. Perhaps Allah will show you something through us that will delight your eyes. Take us forward, relying on the blessing of Allah.{{1}}
blocks.37: The Prophet {{1}} was pleased. He said, go forward, take glad tidings. Allah has promised me one of the two groups. By Allah, it is as if I can see their places of death right now.{{2}}
blocks.38: The Qur’an did not hide one thing here. Not everyone was equally without hesitation.
blocks.40: (The matter of dividing the spoils) is much like that, as your Lord brought you out of your house for the truth, though a group of the believers disliked it. Even after the truth became clear, they dispute with you about it as though they are being driven toward death and are seeing it with their own eyes.{{1}}
blocks.41: A group of the very believers. Not any hypocrites. They had wanted the caravan. Not a fight. The fear was not false.{{1}}
blocks.42: And what they were wanting, the Qur’an told that too.
blocks.44: Remember the time when Allah promised you that one of the two groups would fall into your hands. And you wished that the thorn-free group would come before you. Allah wished to make the truth manifest as truth by His rulings and to cut off the root of the disbelievers.{{1}}
blocks.45: The thorn-free group. Where there is no risk, no battle. Allah wished something else. We too often want the path that is thorn-free. What Allah wants may be hard. The Companions had fear in their hearts. It did not have to be hidden. The Qur’an has written it down, and their standing did not decrease because of it. Having fear is not a fault; standing with fear is itself courage.
blocks.47: On this very road an incident, in which even one soldier was very valuable. Yet two were sent back. Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA) and his father Husayl (RA). On the way to Badr they had been caught by Quraysh.
blocks.49: The only thing that kept me from attending Badr was this. I and my father Husayl (RA) had set out. The disbelievers of Quraysh seized us. They said, you want to go to Muhammad. We said, no, we only want to go to Madinah. Then they took from us a covenant of Allah that we would go back to Madinah and not fight with him. We came to the Messenger of Allah {{1}} and told him everything. He said, go back. We will fulfil their covenant, and seek Allah’s help against them.{{2}}
blocks.50: The covenant was taken by force. With an enemy. Yet the Prophet {{1}} said, go back. We break promises to the little ones most easily. Later I’ll give. I’ll take you tomorrow. I’ll see. He who kept a promise extracted by coercion from an enemy, is our small promise at home smaller than that? One extra soldier was valuable then. A promise is more valuable than that.
blocks.51: By the Wells, the Day Before
blocks.52: Coming near Badr the Prophet {{1}} himself went out. With him Abu Bakr (RA). News of the enemy was needed. An old Bedouin. Cunning in speech. He said, you tell first who you are. The Prophet {{2}} said, you tell first, then we will tell. The old man told all he had heard. In the end he asked, which tribe are you from? He said, we are from one water. The old man kept thinking, which water? The water of Iraq?{{3}}
blocks.53: In the evening he sent ‘Ali (RA), al-Zubayr (RA) and Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA) to the water’s edge at Badr. There some of Quraysh’s water-carriers came. The Companions interrogated them.
blocks.55: At the water of Badr the water-carriers of Quraysh came. Among them was a black slave of Banu al-Hajjaj. The Companions seized him and began asking about Abu Sufyan and his companions. He would say, I have no news of Abu Sufyan; but Abu Jahl, ‘Utbah, Shaybah and Umayyah ibn Khalaf are here. When he said this they would beat him. Then he would say, all right, I will tell about Abu Sufyan. If they let him go and asked again he would say the earlier thing. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} was standing in prayer then. Seeing this, he finished the prayer. He said, by the One in whose hand is my soul, you beat him when he tells you the truth, and let him go when he lies to you! Then the Messenger of Allah {{2}} said, this is the place of death of so-and-so. He was placing his hand on the ground, here and here. Not one of them moved even a little from the place where the hand of the Messenger of Allah {{3}} was placed.{{4}}
blocks.56: Beat if he tells the truth. Let go if he lies. This reverse rule runs in many places among us. At home a child who tells the truth is punished, one who lies gets away. Who broke it? I did. A slap fell. Who broke it? I don’t know. Nothing happened. The Companions wanted to know about Abu Sufyan. The answer was unwelcome, so hands were raised. If we cannot bear an unwelcome truth, we ourselves make liars.
blocks.57: The Prophet {{1}} asked them, how many? They did not know. How many camels are slaughtered? One day nine, one day ten. He said, then nine hundred to a thousand. Then names. ‘Utbah, Shaybah, Abu al-Bakhtari, Hakim ibn Hizam (RA), al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Abu Jahl, Umayyah ibn Khalaf. The Prophet {{2}} turned to the Companions and said, this Makkah has thrown the pieces of its liver before you.{{3}}
blocks.58: The places which the day before he had shown by placing his hand, ‘Umar (RA) later would swear, no one fell outside them.{{1}}
blocks.60: The biggest question of Badr was water. The Prophet {{1}} halted with the army at the first well of Badr. One man stood up. Hubab ibn al-Mundhir (RA). A man experienced in warfare. He said, O Messenger of Allah, is this place fixed by Allah, from which we have no room to advance or retreat? Or is it your opinion, a stratagem of war? The Prophet {{2}} said, no, it is an opinion, a stratagem of war. Hubab said, then this is not the right place. Come, let us go beside the well nearest to Quraysh. I will fill in the remaining wells. We will build a basin over our well and keep water stored. We will drink, they will not get any. The Prophet {{3}} said, you have given the right counsel. At midnight everyone reached there. The remaining wells were filled in, the basin was built.{{4}}
blocks.61: The Prophet {{1}} kept revelation and opinion separate. Which is Allah’s instruction, which is a battle stratagem, an ordinary soldier could ask that. In our homes, offices, madrasahs, is there room for the small to ask this? What you are saying, is it final, or an opinion?
blocks.62: Now Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) stood up. O Messenger of Allah, let us build a shelter for you. Your mount will be ready beside it. We will face the enemy. If Allah gives victory, that is exactly what we want. If it turns out otherwise, you can ride your mount and go to Madinah, to those behind us. Their love is not less than ours. Had they known, they would not have stayed behind. The Prophet {{1}} praised him, made du‘a. On a high place a shelter went up, from where the whole field could be seen. At the door stood Sa‘d (RA), sword in hand. With him a few young men of the Ansar.{{2}}
blocks.63: Sa‘d (RA) was wanting battle. And also keeping a path open for the Prophet’s {{1}} survival. This too is a form of love. Not only thinking of the good days, but thinking for the bad days too. For the person of our home do we keep a preparation for bad days? For illness, for danger, an alternative?
blocks.64: That night rain came from the sky.
blocks.66: Remember when He was making you drowsy to remove your dread, and was sending down water from the sky upon you, to purify you with it, to remove from you the filth of Satan, to fasten your hearts, and to keep your feet firm by it.{{1}}
blocks.67: On the Muslims’ side the sand packed hard, the feet sat firm. On Quraysh’s side the ground became mud, advancing became hard.{{1}}
blocks.68: Sleep on the night before battle. When fear is greatest, Allah then gave sleep.
blocks.70: All of us were asleep, except the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. He was praying under a tree and weeping, until morning.{{2}}
blocks.71: Sleep in everyone’s eyes. Tears in one person’s eyes. The plan was, water, shelter, guard. Yet the night passed in du‘a. We separate work and du‘a, the two. Some only strive, forget du‘a. Some only make du‘a, give up striving.
blocks.73: That day, 17 Ramadan, Friday, second year of the Hijrah. Dawn. Down the dune the Quraysh army was descending. The Prophet {{1}} saw them.{{2}}
blocks.74: He said, O Allah, this Quraysh has come in arrogance to fight against You, against Your Messenger. O Allah, fulfil the help You promised me.{{1}}
blocks.75: Seeing ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah on a red camel among Quraysh, he said, if there is anything good in anyone in this group, it is with the owner of the red camel. Had they obeyed him they would have found the right path. ‘Utbah was truly speaking of going back. He said, O Quraysh, what do you gain by killing Muhammad and his companions? Each of you will look at the face of someone whose face is hateful for him to see. The one who has killed his cousin, or his maternal cousin. Go back. Abu Jahl heard and said, ‘Utbah’s lungs are swollen, with fear. Besides, his son is in their group. ‘Utbah said angrily, today it will be seen whose lungs are swollen.{{1}}
blocks.76: In the meantime some of Quraysh came toward the Prophet’s {{1}} basin to take water. He said, let them be. That day whoever drank from that basin was killed. Only Hakim ibn Hizam (RA) was saved. Later he became Muslim. When he had to swear, he would say, no, by the One who saved me on the day of Badr.{{2}}
blocks.77: The one we think an enemy today, the door of their heart may open tomorrow. At this moment Allah showed each of the two groups the other as few in their eyes.
blocks.79: (O Prophet!) Remember the time when Allah showed you them (that is, the enemies) as few in your dream. Had He shown you them as many, then (O Muslims!) you would have lost courage and fallen into dispute among yourselves about the matter, but Allah (protected you from that). Surely He knows well even what is hidden in the hearts. And remember when you met one another, Allah showed you their number as few in your eyes and showed you as few in their eyes, so that Allah might accomplish a matter that was to be done. All matters are returned to Allah.{{1}}
blocks.80: In the dream the Prophet {{1}} saw the enemy as few. He told the Companions. Courage rose. At the time of facing each other too, each of the two groups saw the other as few. What was to be done, Allah let it be done.{{2}}
blocks.81: The Prophet {{1}} was straightening the rows. In his hand a stick. Sawad ibn Ghaziyyah (RA) was a little ahead of the row. With the stick he gave a light poke at his belly and said, straight, Sawad. Sawad said, O Messenger of Allah, you have hurt me. Allah sent you with truth and justice. Let me take retaliation. The Prophet {{2}} bared his own belly. He said, take. Sawad embraced him. Kissed the belly. The Prophet {{3}} asked, what did you do, Sawad? He said, O Messenger of Allah, what you see before you. I thought, this may perhaps be the last meeting with you. I wanted my body to touch your body. The Prophet {{4}} made du‘a for him.{{5}}
blocks.82: He whom Allah had sent with justice bared his own belly and said, take. Having grown big, can we tell the small, I made a mistake? When a hand has fallen by mistake on a child’s body, when a wife has been scolded, when a harsh word has been said to a subordinate?
blocks.84: The rows were straightened. The Prophet {{1}} went into the shelter with Abu Bakr (RA). No one else was there. Then what happened was one of the deepest du‘as in history.
blocks.86: The Prophet {{1}} turned toward the qiblah. Stretching out both hands he began calling his Lord, O Allah, fulfil for me what You promised me. O Allah, give me what You promised me. O Allah, if this small group of the followers of Islam is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on earth. He kept calling with hands outstretched, facing the qiblah, until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr (RA) came and picked up the cloak and put it on his shoulders. He embraced him from behind. He said, Prophet of Allah, this imploring of your Lord is enough. He will surely fulfil the promise given to you.{{2}}
blocks.89: Remember when you implored your Lord for help, then He responded to your plea, saying, I am sending a force of a thousand angels to your aid, who will come one after another. Allah has given this promise only so that it may be good news for you and so that your hearts may be at ease; help comes from none other than Allah. Surely Allah is Powerful, Wise.{{1}}
blocks.90: After a while the Prophet {{1}} dozed off a little in the shelter. Waking he said, take glad tidings, Abu Bakr (RA). Jibril is coming holding the horse’s rein. Dust on his teeth. And he came out of the shelter wearing armour, reciting a verse. In that verse revealed in Makkah it was said, this group will soon be defeated.{{2}}
blocks.91: ‘Ali (RA) says, when the fighting grew intense, everyone took refuge behind the Prophet {{1}}.
blocks.93: On the day of Badr when the fighting became intense, we took refuge behind the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. He was one of the firmest of people; no one was nearer to the polytheists than he.{{2}}
blocks.94: Abu Bakr (RA) had put the cloak back. Had embraced him from behind. Had said, enough. Are we that kind of person to our loved ones? When the cloak slips from their shoulder do we put it back? And a leader does not mean one who stands at the very back and gives orders. That day the one nearest to the enemy was the greatest man himself.

quiz.q: At the call to catch the caravan, with whom did the Prophet ﷺ say to travel?
o: Those who had asked permission to bring mounts from Madinah’s upper area
Those who had come from Makkah as Muhajirun
Those whose mounts were then ready
Those who had horses with them

quiz.q: What was the number of the Muslim army at Badr?
In the turns of riding, how many rode each camel?
Who were the companions of the Prophet ﷺ in the turns of riding?
Hearing ‘we will walk for you’, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: Whoever’s mount is ready, let them come with us
Not a single dirham of discount
Is he not a man of Badr?
You two are not stronger than I

quiz.q: A father said, ‘I am old, I can’t manage.’ Which scene of the dars is the greatest opposite to this?
o: The Companions’ interrogation at the water’s edge
The Prophet ﷺ not giving up his turn of riding
Hakim ibn Hizam (RA) being saved from the basin’s water
The Prophet’s ﷺ call as he stood beside the well

quiz.q: Whom did Abu Sufyan hire to wake up Quraysh?
quiz.e: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah.

quiz.q: Who gave Quraysh a guarantee in the guise of Suraqah ibn Malik?
Who finally persuaded Umayyah ibn Khalaf to go to Badr?
Who took Banu Zuhrah back?
Why did Abu Jahl not want to turn back even after the caravan was saved?
o: For fear of an attack by Banu Bakr
For fear of what people would say if he turned back

quiz.q: What weakness is caught in the story of Umayyah ibn Khalaf?
o: A wrong decision out of fear despite knowing the truth
Inability to bear an unwelcome truth
Not seeing the face of the household’s people on a day of success
Measuring a person by their weak day

quiz.q: Walking the wrong path knowing the truth for fear of friends’ mockery is like whose story?
‘We will fight on your right, on your left, in front of you and behind you’; who said this?
‘If you go into the sea we will go too’; who said this on behalf of the Ansar?
quiz.e: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir; Sahih Muslim 1779.

quiz.q: The verse did not hide the Companions’ fear; what is the lesson in this?
o: Standing with fear is itself courage
There will be room for the small to ask

quiz.q: What was the reason for turning Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA) and his father back from Badr?
o: Keeping the covenant given to Quraysh
Being sent back with the duty of looking after Madinah

quiz.q: Repeatedly breaking a promise to a small boy saying ‘later I’ll give’ is the opposite of which incident in the dars?
o: ‘Umayr throwing away the dates in his hand
Hudhayfah and Husayl (RA) keeping their covenant
Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr’s (RA) words, saying ‘he is my brother’

quiz.q: At the water’s edge, beaten if one told the truth, released if one lied; what is the consequence of this?
o: Even household service becomes the reward of Badr
Love means preparing for bad days

quiz.q: At home the boy who said ‘I broke it’ got a slap, the boy who said ‘I don’t know’ was let off. Which scene of the dars does this recall?
o: Abu Hudhayfah’s (RA) gloom beside the well
Beating the slave who told the truth at the water’s edge
Children being taught to write by the captives

quiz.q: Who gave the counsel to change the place of the well?
Who gave the proposal to build a shelter for the Prophet ﷺ?
Who was awake on the night of Badr, praying and weeping?
What does Hubab ibn al-Mundhir’s (RA) question ‘is this revelation or opinion?’ teach?
o: Giving one’s dear ones first in a place of risk
The effort is mine, the result is Allah’s
The difference between revelation and opinion can be asked about
Keeping promises even to the small

quiz.q: What does Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh’s (RA) proposal to keep a mount ready teach?
o: Admitting mistakes even to the small
Thinking also of bad days is love
Getting up leaving the small dates in the hand
Serving the subordinate good food first

quiz.q: What lesson does the dars take from the plan of the night of Badr and the all-night du‘a?
o: Room for the small to ask
Keeping the limit of justice amid the pain of dear ones
Keeping promises even to the small
quiz.e: Musnad Ahmad 1023; Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir.

quiz.q: An office subordinate asked, ‘Is this word of yours final, or an opinion?’ The lesson of which incident of the dars applies here?
o: Sa‘d’s (RA) proposal to build the shelter
Hubab’s question and the Prophet’s ﷺ agreement

quiz.q: Someone only strives and forgets du‘a, someone only makes du‘a and gives up striving. Which night can be compared?
o: The night of Badr: there was a plan, there was du‘a too
The night of ‘Atikah’s dream, when the call came in Makkah
The night in which the Prophet ﷺ did not sleep because of ‘Abbas’s (RA) groaning
The night in which al-Aswad heard the sound of weeping

quiz.q: What was the date and day of Badr?
Who asked retaliation from the Prophet ﷺ while the rows were being straightened?
Who drank from Quraysh’s basin and was still saved?
From the incident of Sawad ibn Ghaziyyah (RA), what lesson for elders?
o: When wrong, say even to the small, I made a mistake
Giving one’s dear ones first at a place of risk
Keeping promises even to the small
Hugging a weary loved one and giving reassurance

quiz.q: A father said on touching his child by mistake, ‘I made a mistake, what do you want?’ Like which scene?
o: The Prophet ﷺ saying ‘take’ to Sawad
‘Abd al-Rahman telling Umayyah to sit down
Informing Abu al-Bakhtari of al-Mujadhdhar’s prohibition

quiz.q: What can be learned from Abu Bakr’s (RA) putting back the cloak?
o: Putting forward one’s own household’s people first at a place of risk
Throwing away the small dates in the hand
Serving the subordinate good food first
Hugging a weary loved one and giving reassurance

porbos.title: The Call of Paradise • Three Pairs of Swords • Help From the Sky • The End of Abu Jahl • Flight, and Surrender • Bilal’s Call • Beside the Well • The Martyrs, and a Mother’s Question • On the Road to Madinah

blocks.1: Quraysh was advancing. The Prophet {{1}} stopped the Companions. Until I go ahead, no one will go forward.
blocks.3: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} said, until I go ahead, none of you shall move forward toward anything. The polytheists came near. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} said, rise to a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth. ‘Umayr ibn al-Humam al-Ansari said, O Messenger of Allah, a Paradise whose breadth is the heavens and the earth? He said, yes. ‘Umayr said, wow, wow! The Messenger of Allah {{3}} said, what makes you say wow, wow? He said, no, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, only the hope that I may be one of its people. He said, you are one of its people. Then ‘Umayr took out a few dates from his quiver and began to eat them. Then he said, if I live until I finish eating these dates of mine, that is indeed a long life! He threw away the dates in his hand, then fought them, until he was martyred.{{4}}
blocks.4: Dates. A very small thing. But to him even the time of eating them was then a long life. We too have dates in our hands. A little more sleep, a little more scrolling, a little more chatting. Putting down the work in hand at the adhan is a small form of ‘Umayr’s throwing away of the dates.
blocks.6: Now into the middle of the field came out three heroes of Quraysh. ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, his brother Shaybah, his son al-Walid. He called out, who will fight? Three young men of the Ansar stepped forward.
blocks.8: ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah came forward, behind him his son and his brother. He called out, who will fight? Some young men of the Ansar advanced toward him. He said, who are you? When they identified themselves he said, we have no need of you. We wanted our cousins. Then the Messenger of Allah {{1}} said, rise Hamzah (RA), rise ‘Ali (RA), rise ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Harith (RA). Hamzah (RA) advanced toward ‘Utbah, I toward Shaybah. Between ‘Ubaydah (RA) and al-Walid two blows were exchanged, each seriously wounding the other. Then we turned on al-Walid, killed him, and carried off ‘Ubaydah (RA).{{2}}
blocks.9: His own uncle, his own cousin, another of his own clan. In the first face-to-face fight the Prophet {{1}} put forward the very people of his own blood. Hamzah (RA) and ‘Ali (RA) finished off their own opponents. ‘Ubaydah (RA) and his opponent seriously wounded each other. Then ‘Ali (RA) and Hamzah (RA) went and finished that man off, and brought ‘Ubaydah (RA) back.{{2}}
blocks.10: The Qur’an has spoken of this fight too.
blocks.12: These (the believers and the disbelievers) are two adversaries who dispute concerning their Lord. So (the decision will be thus:) for those who have disbelieved garments of fire have been cut out. Boiling water will be poured over their heads.{{1}}
blocks.13: Who these two parties are, Abu Dharr (RA) used to swear, those who fought face to face on the day of Badr.{{1}}
blocks.14: ‘Ubaydah (RA) was laid down beside the place where the Prophet {{1}} stood. He placed his cheek on the Prophet’s {{2}} foot. He said, had Abu Talib seen me, he would have understood, I am the most deserving of that poem of his: ‘We will not give him up, until we fall prostrate before him, and forget our own children and wives’. Then ‘Ubaydah (RA) died. The Prophet {{3}} said, I bear witness, you are a martyr.{{4}}
blocks.15: One’s own blood in a place of risk. We call our dear ones to a place of gain, others to a place of risk. The Prophet {{1}} did the opposite. At the other end ‘Ubaydah ibn Sa‘id fell before al-Zubayr (RA), covered in full armour, only two eyes visible. Al-Zubayr (RA) struck his eye with a short spear, he died. The Prophet {{2}} asked for that spear. Later Abu Bakr (RA), ‘Umar (RA), ‘Uthman (RA) asked for it one after another. Finally it was with ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA), until he was killed.{{3}}
blocks.16: One spear. From the Messenger’s hand through the hands of three caliphs, through ‘Ali’s (RA) family, to the house of al-Zubayr’s (RA) son. Badr never became the past for them.
blocks.18: Ahead, three times the number. Behind, the sky. In Surah Al ‘Imran Allah said:
blocks.20: Allah helped you at Badr when you were utterly without resources. So keep (only) the fear of Allah in your hearts, so that you may be grateful. (At the time of Badr) when you were saying to the believers, is it not enough for you that your Lord will help you with three thousand angels sent down? Yes indeed, if you are patient and adopt taqwa, and they come upon you at this very moment suddenly, your Lord will send five thousand angels to your aid, bearing distinctive marks.{{1}}
blocks.21: In Surah al-Anfal it is said a thousand. Here three thousand. And five thousand with conditions: patience, taqwa, and a sudden attack by the enemy.{{1}}
blocks.22: What did the angels do? A small scene seen through one Muslim’s eyes.
blocks.24: That day a Muslim was chasing a polytheist. Suddenly he heard the sound of a whip from above and the voice of a horseman, advance, Haizum! He looked at the polytheist ahead, and saw he had fallen on his back. He looked at him, and saw his nose was smashed, his face split as by a whip stroke, and all of it had turned green. The Ansari came and told the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. He said, you have spoken the truth. That is from the reinforcement of the third heaven. That day they killed seventy and took seventy captive.{{2}}
blocks.25: Then the Prophet {{1}} picked up a handful of gravelly soil and threw it toward Quraysh. He said, may the faces be disfigured.{{2}}
blocks.27: So (O Muslims! in truth) you did not kill them (that is, the disbelievers); rather Allah killed them, and (O Prophet!) when you threw (the soil) at them, it was not you who threw; rather Allah threw, and (He did it by your hands) so that He might give the believers a good reward through it. Surely Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.{{1}}
blocks.28: The soil in that fist reached the eyes and faces of every disbeliever. An uproar broke out in the enemy army.{{1}}
blocks.29: A handful of gravel does not stop an army. It stopped because Allah wished it. The effort is mine, the result is Allah’s. This one sentence reduces arrogance and reduces despair at the same time.
blocks.31: A thick crowd in the middle of the field. Inside, Abu Jahl. All around people were saying, no one will be able to reach Abu al-Hakam.{{1}}
blocks.32: That morning he had made du‘a. O Allah, whoever among us cuts kinship the most, and whoever has brought us what is unfamiliar, destroy him this very morning.{{1}}
blocks.33: That very du‘a was accepted. Against himself.
blocks.35: (O disbelievers!) If you were seeking a decision, the decision has already come to you. Now if you desist, it will be better for you. And if you do again that same thing (that you have been doing so far), we too will do again the same (as we have just done), and then your group will be of no use to you, however large its number. Remember, Allah is with the believers.{{1}}
blocks.36: And it was two boys who stopped him.
blocks.38: I was standing in the row on the day of Badr. Looking to my right and left I saw two boys of the Ansar, young in age. I thought, would that I were between two stronger men than these! Then one poked me and said, uncle, do you know Abu Jahl? I said, yes, nephew, what do you need from him? He said, I have been told he abuses the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. By the One in whose hand is my soul, if I see him, my shadow will not leave his shadow until the one of us whose death is earlier dies. I was amazed. ... Shortly after, I saw Abu Jahl going about among the people. I said, there, that is the one you were looking for. The two of them leapt at him with their swords, struck him, until they killed him.{{2}}
blocks.39: They were Mu‘adh ibn ‘Amr ibn al-Jamuh (RA) and Mu‘adh ibn ‘Afra’ (RA). Seeing blood on both swords the Prophet {{1}} said, you both killed him. The word of the two boys was one: one who abuses the Messenger of Allah {{2}}, my shadow will not mix with his. Hearing that he abuses, love awoke. How dear is the Prophet {{3}} to our teenagers?
blocks.40: The Prophet {{1}} asked, who will see what Abu Jahl did?
blocks.42: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} said, who will see what Abu Jahl did? Ibn Mas‘ud went and saw that Afra’s two sons had struck him until he had gone cold. He seized his beard. He said, are you Abu Jahl? He said, is there anyone above a man you have killed? Or he said, a man whom his own people have killed?{{2}}
blocks.43: There was still a little life in him. Ibn Mas‘ud said, Allah has humiliated you. He said, whose victory is it today? He said, Allah’s and His Messenger’s. The Prophet {{1}} on hearing the news said, by the One besides Whom there is no deity, truly? He made him swear three times. Then he praised Allah.{{2}}
blocks.44: Whoever seeks a decision today thinks the ruling will go in their favour.
blocks.46: Quraysh’s ranks broke. No one could flee in good order. Each ran wherever they could, into the clefts of the mountains, the passes, the valleys. On the road to Makkah each returned when they could, terrified.{{1}}
blocks.47: Seventy killed, and seventy captured; many of the captives were leading men of Makkah. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf (RA) was carrying several coats of mail taken from Quraysh. Umayyah ibn Khalaf saw him and said, I am better than these coats of mail of yours, will you take me? ‘Abd al-Rahman threw down the coats of mail. He began walking holding the hands of Umayyah and his son.{{1}}
blocks.48: Throwing away loot to save one captive. We too sometimes forget, the person in hand is greater than the thing in hand. That day ‘Abbas ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib was also taken captive. An Ansari had brought him. ‘Abbas (RA) said, by Allah, this man did not capture me. I was captured by a bald, handsome man, on a black-and-white horse. I do not see him in this group. The Ansari said, O Messenger of Allah, I captured him. The Prophet {{1}} said, be quiet. Allah has helped you with a noble angel.{{2}}
blocks.50: Umayyah ibn Khalaf. In Makkah he used to torture Bilal (RA), to make him give up Islam.{{1}}
blocks.51: That very Umayyah at Badr fell into ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf’s (RA) hands, a captive.
blocks.53: I had written an agreement with Umayyah ibn Khalaf that he would look after my family and companions in Makkah, and I would look after his family and companions in Madinah. When I mentioned (my name) ‘al-Rahman’ he said, I do not know al-Rahman. Write with your name that you had in the Jahiliyyah. I wrote ‘Abd ‘Amr. On the day of Badr when the people had fallen asleep I went toward the mountain to secure him. Bilal (RA) saw him. He went and stood at a gathering of the Ansar and said, Umayyah ibn Khalaf! If he is saved, I will not be saved! With him a group of the Ansar chased after us. Thinking they would catch up, I left his son behind for them, so that they would be occupied. They killed him. Still they did not give up following us. Umayyah was a heavy man. When they caught up I said to him, kneel down. He knelt. I threw myself over him, to protect him. They thrust swords through underneath me and killed him. The sword of one of them struck my foot. ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf (RA) used to show us that mark on the top of his foot.{{1}}
blocks.54: Bilal’s (RA) mouth that day had one word. If he is saved, I will not be saved. The one who was tortured in Makkah, today at his call the Ansar ran. The call was, O Ansar of Allah! ‘Abd al-Rahman (RA) would say later, may Allah have mercy on Bilal (RA). My coats of mail went, and my captive went too.{{1}}
blocks.55: We measure people by their weakest day. Whom we think poor today, uneducated, ordinary, when their day with Allah is coming, we do not know.
blocks.56: That day the Prophet {{1}} had told the Companions, do not kill any of Banu Hashim, do not kill Abu al-Bakhtari, do not kill ‘Abbas (RA). They have been brought out by force. Abu al-Bakhtari had not harmed the Prophet {{2}} in Makkah. Mujadhdhar ibn Ziyad (RA) said to him, you are forbidden to be killed; not your companion. He said, then he and I will die together. He died in the fight.{{3}}
blocks.57: Even on the battlefield the Prophet {{1}} had not forgotten who in Makkah had harmed him less. In anger we wipe out ten years of favour in one sentence. To the person of our home in one moment we say, what have you done in life?
blocks.59: The battle was over. On the field the bodies of Quraysh’s leaders. The Prophet {{1}} gave an order. The bodies of twenty-four leaders were thrown into an old well of Badr.
blocks.61: On the day of Badr the Prophet {{1}} ordered that the bodies of twenty-four chiefs of Quraysh be thrown into a well of Badr. The well was foul, filthy. ... On the third day he stood at the edge of the well. He began calling them by their names and their fathers’ names, O so-and-so son of so-and-so, O so-and-so son of so-and-so, would it please you if you had obeyed Allah and His Messenger? We have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you found what your Lord promised you to be true? ‘Umar (RA) said, O Messenger of Allah, what are you speaking to, bodies without souls? The Messenger of Allah {{2}} said, by the One in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, you do not hear what I say better than they.{{3}}
blocks.62: ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah was being dragged toward the well. The Prophet {{1}} looked at his son Abu Hudhayfah (RA).
blocks.64: The Prophet {{1}} looked at Abu Hudhayfah’s (RA) face and saw he was gloomy, the colour of his face changed. He said, Hudhayfah, it seems something has entered you about your father? He said, no, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I have no doubt about my father, or about his place of death. But I used to know my father as a man of judgement, forbearance and virtue. I hoped these would guide him to Islam. Now seeing what has befallen him, and remembering the disbelief in which he died, after what I had hoped for him, it grieves me. Then the Messenger of Allah {{2}} made a du‘a of good for him, and said, good.{{3}}
blocks.65: One who on the day of victory sees the shadow on a single boy’s face also sees the shadow on the faces of those of the household. On days of success we forget to read the faces of the people at home. Abu Hudhayfah’s (RA) grief was for his father’s death upon disbelief. The Prophet {{1}} did not count even that grief as an offence. He made du‘a.{{2}}
blocks.66: The Martyrs, and a Mother’s Question
blocks.67: Fourteen were martyred on the Muslims’ side at Badr. Six Muhajirun, eight Ansar.{{1}}
blocks.68: Muhajirun: ‘Ubaydah ibn al-Harith (RA), ‘Umayr ibn Abi Waqqas, Dhu al-Shimalayn ‘Umayr ibn ‘Abd ‘Amr, Safwan ibn Bayda’, ‘Aqil ibn al-Bukayr and ‘Umar’s (RA) freed slave Mihja‘ (RA). Ansar: Sa‘d ibn Khaythamah, Mubashshir ibn ‘Abd al-Mundhir, Yazid ibn al-Harith, ‘Umayr ibn al-Humam (RA), Rafi‘ ibn al-Mu‘alla, Harithah ibn Suraqah (RA), ‘Awf and Mu‘awwidh, the two sons of ‘Afra’. ‘Umayr, the younger brother of Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA), was only sixteen.{{1}}
blocks.69: The first martyr Mihja‘ (RA). Then Harithah ibn Suraqah (RA). Harithah was then a boy. He was not in the battle line, he was among the spectators. He had gone to drink water from the basin. An unknown arrow came and struck him.{{1}}
blocks.71: Umm al-Rubayyi‘ bint al-Bara’ (RA), the mother of Harithah ibn Suraqah (RA), came to the Prophet {{1}} and said, O Prophet, will you not tell me about Harithah? On the day of Badr a stray arrow struck him. If he is in Paradise I will be patient; and if it is otherwise I will exhaust myself in weeping for him. He said, O mother of Harithah, Paradise is not one; there are many Paradises. Your son has attained the highest Firdaws.{{2}}
blocks.72: To a grieving mother he did not give advice. He gave news. In the face of grief we give advice most easily. Be patient. It is Allah’s will. The Prophet {{1}} gave news that lifts the weight from the chest.
blocks.74: Sending the news of victory, the Prophet {{1}} sent two ahead. Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) to the lower part of Madinah, ‘Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA) to the upper part. When Zayd reached Madinah, people were then levelling the soil on the grave of Ruqayyah bint Rasulillah (RA).{{2}}
blocks.75: Ruqayyah (RA). The Prophet’s {{1}} daughter. The wife of ‘Uthman (RA). At the time of Badr she was ill. ‘Uthman (RA) did not go to Badr. The Prophet {{2}} had told him to stay with his wife.
blocks.77: And what of his absence from Badr? His wife was the daughter of the Messenger of Allah {{1}}, and she was ill. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} said to him, you will have the reward of one who attended Badr, and his share.{{3}}
blocks.78: The reward of a warrior of Badr and a share of the spoils. Both. Instead of sitting at an ill wife’s bedside. One who serves at home is also a man of Badr. The Prophet {{1}} gave it a name, the reward of Badr. Who in our home is fighting such a Badr today, we do not know. Is their name in our ledger of gratitude?
blocks.79: The Prophet {{1}} was returning with captives and spoils. Halting at a dune of al-Safra’ he divided the spoils equally. At Rawha’ the leaders of Madinah came and offered congratulations. Salamah ibn Salamah (RA) said, what congratulations? We only fought some bald old men, big like camels. We slaughtered them. The Prophet {{2}} said with a smile, nephew, those were the leaders of this people. Usayd ibn Hudayr (RA) came forward and said, O Messenger of Allah, all praise is for Allah who has cooled your eyes. By Allah, had I known you would have to face the enemy I would not have stayed behind. I thought it was a caravan. The Prophet {{3}} said, you speak the truth.{{4}}
blocks.80: Salamah’s blunt words the Prophet {{1}} took lightly with a smile. He also accepted Usayd’s excuse and said, you speak the truth. When someone is late coming to our home we find fault first. We do not lend an ear to hear the excuse.

Ibn Hisham, Sirat al-Nabi (Bengali), vol. 2, p. 313. Sirah-based.

quiz.q: Hearing of Paradise, what did ‘Umayr ibn al-Humam (RA) throw away before plunging into the fight?
o: A necklace given by his mother

quiz.q: Of what could ‘Umayr’s throwing away the dates be a small form today?
o: Not replying in a moment of anger
Admitting a mistake to one’s child
Putting down the work in hand at the adhan
Remembering a person’s sacrifice along with their mistake

quiz.q: In the first duel, whom did the Prophet ﷺ put forward?
o: ‘Ali (RA), al-Zubayr (RA) and Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA)

quiz.q: The Prophet ﷺ sent the Ansari youths back and put forward relatives; what is the lesson?
o: Love means preparing even for bad days
Not measuring people by their weak day
The effort is mine, the result is Allah’s
In a place of risk give one’s own household first

quiz.q: What is the lesson of the verse ‘you did not throw; rather Allah threw’?
o: Tears instead of excuses when a mistake is caught
The effort is mine, the result is Allah’s
Not forgetting a person’s sacrifice because of their mistake

quiz.q: Who were the two boys who struck Abu Jahl?
Before saying ‘Allah decide’ in a quarrel, check one’s own position; this lesson is from whose du‘a?
o: Abu Rafi‘’s (RA) announcement at the room
quiz.e: Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Kathir; Tawdih al-Qur’an, 8:19.

quiz.q: What did ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf (RA) throw away for Umayyah?
o: The camel of his share of spoils

quiz.q: Who gave Umayyah ibn Khalaf away saying ‘if he is saved, I will not be saved’?
What does the Ansar running at one call of Bilal (RA) teach?
o: Judging people by their weak day is not right
Giving one’s own household first at a place of risk
Even household service is the reward of Badr

quiz.q: Wiping out a wife’s ten years of service in one sentence in anger is the opposite of the lesson of which incident?
o: Giving bread to Abu ‘Aziz and eating dates themselves
The order not to kill Abu al-Bakhtari
Bared belly and saying ‘take’ to Sawad

quiz.q: Reading Abu Hudhayfah’s (RA) face beside the well, what did the Prophet ﷺ teach?
o: The effort is mine, the result is Allah’s
Love awakening on hearing the Messenger abused
Reading the faces of household people even on a day of success

quiz.q: On a day of success one person of the household sits silently. Whose face did the Prophet ﷺ read?
o: The martyred son of Umm al-Rubayyi‘

quiz.q: How many Companions were martyred at Badr?
To a grieving mother, ‘be patient’ is our habit. What news did the Prophet ﷺ give to console Umm al-Rubayyi‘?
o: I bear witness that you are a martyr
I will teach you something better than what you asked
Your son has attained the highest Firdaws
Is he not a man of Badr?

quiz.q: In reply to the congratulations at Rawha’, what did Salamah ibn Salamah say?
o: We only wanted to catch the caravan, not war
We only fought bald old men
The angels did all the fighting for us
We did not set out for the spoils

quiz.q: Who went to the upper part of Madinah with the glad tidings of victory?
‘Uthman (RA) got the reward and share without going to Badr; what is the lesson?
o: Household service too is a deed of reward like Badr
In the face of grief, not advice but glad tidings
Pain comes out under another name when weeping is forbidden
Keeping promises even to the small

quiz.q: Leaving everything to nurse a wife in illness recalls which Companion of the dars?

porbos.title: The Prisoners’ Homes • The Ransom Decision • An Uncle’s Groans, a Daughter’s Necklace • Mourning in Makkah • ‘Umayr ibn Wahb • The Rank of the Men of Badr • After the Treaty Was Broken • Fatimah’s Home • Final Word

blocks.1: On the way back two men were sentenced to death. al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and ‘Uqbah ibn Abi Mu‘ayt. These were not just prisoners of war. For years in Makkah they had been the leaders of the persecution of the Muslims. In today’s language, war criminals.{{1}}
blocks.2: The remaining prisoners the Prophet {{1}} distributed among the Companions’ homes. He said, treat them well.{{2}}
blocks.4: I was brought from Badr with a group of the Ansar. When they brought their morning and evening meals, they gave me bread and ate dates themselves; because the Messenger of Allah {{1}} had charged them concerning us. If a piece of bread came into anyone’s hand, they would give it to me. I felt ashamed and handed it back, and they would hand it back to me, without even touching it.{{2}}
blocks.5: Abu ‘Aziz was Mus‘ab ibn ‘Umayr’s (RA) own brother. When the captive was being taken, Mus‘ab (RA) had said to that Ansari, tie him up tightly. His mother is wealthy. Abu ‘Aziz said, brother, is this your charge? Mus‘ab (RA) said, he is my brother, not you. Later his mother ransomed him for four thousand dirhams.{{1}}
blocks.6: Giving a piece of bread to a captive instead of eating it oneself. The weight of a single charge. What do we put on the plate of the person who works in our home? The shop boy, the helper at the house, the employee under us? Among the prisoners was Suhayl ibn ‘Amr. A well-known orator of Quraysh, with a split lower lip. ‘Umar (RA) said, O Messenger of Allah, give me permission, let me pull out his two front teeth. Then he will never again be able to stand up and speak against you. The Prophet {{1}} said, I will not disfigure his mouth. Then Allah would disfigure mine, though I am a prophet. He also said another thing, perhaps he will stand in a place for which you will not blame him.{{2}}
blocks.7: Not even a captive enemy’s mouth was allowed to be disfigured by the one who held the power to decide that day. In anger we do not hesitate to jab at someone’s face, body, name. Many years later, at the Prophet’s {{1}} passing, when a wave of apostasy rose in Makkah, Suhayl ibn ‘Amr (RA) delivered a sermon with that very same mouth. He held the people of Makkah firm upon the religion.{{2}}
blocks.8: The one we blame today, where they will stand tomorrow, we do not know.
blocks.10: Now the question, what will happen to the prisoners?
blocks.12: The Messenger of Allah {{1}} said to Abu Bakr (RA) and ‘Umar (RA), what is your view about these prisoners? Abu Bakr (RA) said, O Prophet, they are cousins, relatives. I think you should take ransom from them. That will be a strength for us against the disbelievers. And perhaps Allah will guide them to Islam. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} said, Ibn al-Khattab, what is your view? I said, no, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I do not think what Abu Bakr (RA) thinks. I want you to give us the opportunity, so that we strike their necks. ... For these are the leaders of disbelief, the commanders of disbelief. The Messenger of Allah {{3}} liked what Abu Bakr (RA) said, and did not like what I said. The next morning I went and found the Messenger of Allah {{4}} and Abu Bakr (RA) sitting and weeping. I said, O Messenger of Allah, tell me why you and your companion are weeping. If I find weeping I will weep; if not, I will pretend to weep because of your weeping. The Messenger of Allah {{5}} said, I weep for what has come before me because your companions took ransom. Their punishment was shown to me, nearer than this tree.{{6}}
blocks.13: Abu Bakr’s (RA) words are gentle. ‘Umar’s (RA) words are hard. The Prophet {{1}} liked Abu Bakr’s (RA) words. Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) even while the prisoners were being taken stood at the door of the Prophet’s {{2}} tent with his sword in his hand. The Prophet {{3}} saw a shadow of displeasure on his face. He said, Sa‘d (RA), it seems the people’s doing does not please you. Sa‘d (RA) said, yes, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah. This was Allah’s first blow upon shirk. To me, finishing them off was dearer than keeping prisoners.{{4}}
blocks.14: Then the verses of Allah were revealed:
blocks.16: It is not fitting for any prophet to have prisoners until he has shed blood widely in the land (so that their influence is completely finished). You desire the goods of the world, and Allah desires the Hereafter (good for you). Allah is Mighty and Wise. Had there not been a decree from Allah written beforehand, a great punishment would have befallen you for the path you have taken. So enjoy the spoils you have gained as good lawful wealth, and fear Allah. Surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.17: Consultation, then decision. After the decision, displeasure in the verse. And right after that, forgiveness: what you have gained is good lawful wealth.{{1}}
blocks.18: The part of the verses that follows had a message for the prisoners:
blocks.20: O Prophet! Say to the prisoners in your hands (and those who have expressed the wish to accept Islam), if Allah sees any good in your hearts, He will give you something better than what has been taken from you (as ransom), and will forgive you. Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.21: For those who had no money for ransom, another way was arranged.
blocks.23: Some of the captives of Badr had no ransom. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} fixed their ransom: they would teach the children of the Ansar to write.{{2}}
blocks.24: Here the ransom is not money. It is knowledge. From a captive’s mouth, the first writing lessons of Madinah’s children.{{1}}
blocks.25: The Prophet {{1}} took counsel. A decision was made. Then two friends sat and wept. When our mistake is caught we offer excuses. There, tears.
blocks.26: An Uncle’s Groans, a Daughter’s Necklace
blocks.27: Among the prisoners was the Prophet’s {{1}} uncle ‘Abbas (RA). That night the Prophet {{2}} could not sleep. The Companions asked, O Messenger of Allah, why are you not sleeping? He said, I hear the groaning of my uncle ‘Abbas (RA), in tight bonds. Someone went and loosened the bonds. The groaning stopped. The Prophet {{3}} slept.{{4}}
blocks.28: Some Ansar came and said, O Messenger of Allah, we release the ransom of our sister’s son ‘Abbas (RA).
blocks.30: Some men of the Ansar asked permission from the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. They said, O Messenger of Allah, allow us to leave the ransom of our sister’s son ‘Abbas (RA). He said, no, you will not leave him even one dirham of it.{{2}}
blocks.31: At night, sleep forbidden over an uncle’s pain. By day, not even one dirham of concession. The heart melts at the pain of one’s own. But the limit of justice cannot be broken for one’s own. ‘Abbas (RA) said, where will I get so much money? The Prophet {{1}} said, where is the money that you and Umm al-Fadl (RA) hid and left behind? ‘Abbas (RA) said in astonishment, by Allah, I know that you are the Messenger of Allah. No one knew this except me and Umm al-Fadl (RA).{{2}}
blocks.32: Ransom began to arrive from Makkah. Zaynab, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (RA), sent it for the release of her husband Abu al-‘As (RA). With it, a necklace.
blocks.34: When the people of Makkah sent ransom for their prisoners, Zaynab (RA) sent some wealth as the ransom of Abu al-‘As (RA). And she sent a necklace of hers as well. The necklace was Khadijah’s (RA); when sending her to Abu al-‘As’s (RA) house, Khadijah (RA) had adorned her with it. The Messenger of Allah {{1}} saw the necklace and became extremely tender. He said, if you think it right, release her captive and return to her what is hers. They said, yes. The Messenger of Allah {{2}} had taken a pledge from Abu al-‘As (RA) that he would let Zaynab (RA) go on her way. He sent Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) and an Ansari. He said, stay at Batn Yajij, and when Zaynab (RA) passes, take her along and come to me with her.{{3}}
blocks.35: Khadijah’s (RA) necklace. Many years before, on a wedding day, a mother had adorned her daughter with it with her own hands. Khadijah (RA) is no more, for some years now. But seeing the necklace, the Prophet’s {{1}} heart melted. He did not release on his own. He said to the Companions, if you think it right. The Companions said, yes. Abu al-‘As (RA) was freed. He gave his word that he would let Zaynab (RA) go to Madinah. He kept that word.{{2}}
blocks.36: The one who is no more, a necklace made us remember her. And the one who is still in the house? Toiling silently every day, asking for nothing? How many times have we told that person, I have not forgotten you? How many days has it gone unsaid? A few years later the Prophet {{1}} spoke about that son-in-law.
blocks.38: I heard the Messenger of Allah {{1}} speak of a son-in-law of his from Banu ‘Abd Shams. He praised him as a son-in-law, and spoke well. He said, he spoke to me and told the truth; he promised me and kept it.{{2}}
blocks.40: The first to bring the news to Makkah was Haysuman ibn ‘Abdillah al-Khuza‘i. He began to name names. ‘Utbah, Shaybah, Abu al-Hakam, Umayyah, Zam‘ah, Nubayh, Munabbih, Abu al-Bakhtari. Hearing the names of the leaders, Safwan ibn Umayyah said, he has gone mad. Ask him about me. They asked, what news of Safwan? He said, there he is, sitting in the Hijr. I saw his father and his brother die. Quraysh said, no one will weep. When Muhammad and his companions hear, they will rejoice. And no hurry over the ransom of the prisoners either. Three sons of blind al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib had died. One night he heard the sound of weeping and sent his slave, go and see, has Quraysh lifted the ban? The slave came back and said, a woman is weeping for her lost camel. Al-Aswad could not hold himself. Poetry burst out: do not weep for a camel, weep for Badr.{{1}}
blocks.41: Where weeping is forbidden, all pain comes out in the name of a lost camel. In our homes too there is such a person, who weeps under the pretext of something else. What has really happened, no one asks.
blocks.42: Abu Lahab did not go to Badr. In his place he had sent al-‘As ibn Hisham, in return for a debt of four thousand dirhams. When the news came, Abu Rafi‘ (RA), the slave of ‘Abbas (RA), was sitting in the hujrah of Zamzam. Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith came back and said to Abu Lahab, we saw white men, on piebald horses, between heaven and earth. Nothing was holding firm before them. Abu Rafi‘ (RA) raised the pole of the hujrah and said, by Allah, those are angels. Abu Lahab punched him in the face, threw him to the ground and sat on him. Umm al-Fadl (RA) lifted a pole and struck his head such a blow that his head split open. She said, you thought him weak because his master is not here? Abu Lahab went away humiliated. Not even seven nights passed. He died of a pustule called al-‘Adasah. His sons, out of fear of contagion, left his corpse for three days.{{1}}
blocks.43: A proud person, on receiving news of defeat, vents anger on someone weaker than themselves. We too, insulted at the office, return home and vent our anger on wife and children.
blocks.45: Some days after Badr, Safwan ibn Umayyah was sitting in the Hijr in Makkah. His father and brother had died at Badr. ‘Umayr ibn Wahb came and sat beside him. In Makkah he had tormented the Prophet {{1}} and the Companions a great deal. His son Wahb was then a prisoner in Madinah. Talk turned to the leaders thrown into the well. Safwan said, there is no joy in living after them. ‘Umayr said, true. Were it not for my debt, were it not for the worry of providing for my children, I would go to Muhammad and kill him. And my son is also a prisoner in their hands. Safwan seized the opportunity. He said, your debt is mine, and your children’s responsibility is mine too. No one will know of this. ‘Umayr sharpened his sword and smeared it with poison. Then he reached Madinah. The moment he made his camel sit at the mosque door, ‘Umar (RA) noticed him. ‘Umar (RA) was then discussing Badr. He saw that ‘Umayr had a sword on his shoulder. ‘Umar (RA) went and said to the Prophet {{2}}, the enemy of Allah, ‘Umayr ibn Wahb, has come with a sword hanging. The Prophet {{3}} said, bring him to me. ‘Umar (RA) took hold of the strap of his sword, twisted it around his neck and brought him. The Prophet {{4}} said, ‘Umar (RA), let him go. ‘Umayr, come close. ‘Umayr came close and said, good morning. The Prophet {{5}} said, Allah has given us a greeting that is the salutation of the people of Paradise. Why have you come? He said, for my son who is a prisoner in your hands. Have mercy on him. The Prophet {{6}} said, why the sword on your shoulder? ‘Umayr said, may Allah ruin swords, what use have they been to us? The Prophet {{7}} said, tell the truth, why have you come? He said, I have come only for my son. Then the Prophet {{8}} said, no. You and Safwan ibn Umayyah were sitting in the Hijr talking about the Quraysh thrown into the well. You said, were it not for debt and children I would go and kill Muhammad. Safwan has taken on your debt and the responsibility for your children, on the condition that you kill me. But Allah stands between you and your wish. ‘Umayr was stunned. He said, I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah. All the news from the sky that you used to tell us, the revelation that came, we rejected it. But this no one knew except me and Safwan. By Allah, I am certain that no one but Allah informed you of this. All praise belongs to Allah, who guided me to Islam.{{9}}
blocks.46: The Prophet {{1}} said to the Companions, teach your brother the religion, have him recite the Qur’an, and release his captive son. They did so. The one whom ‘Umar (RA) had brought in a moment before by the strap of his sword is now a brother. ‘Umayr went back to Makkah. This time no sword in hand; an invitation in his mouth. Through his hand many embraced Islam. On hearing of ‘Umayr’s Islam, Safwan swore he would never speak to him and never do him any favour.{{2}}
blocks.47: The greatest thing in this event is not the Prophet’s {{1}} knowing a secret. The greatest thing is that to the one he had the most reason to fear he said, come close. Whoever we assume to be a criminal, we do not leave even a crack of the door open for. Yet the one who had a poisoned sword in his hand returned one day to Makkah on behalf of the Prophet {{2}}, carrying the call to Islam.
blocks.48: The Rank of the Men of Badr
blocks.49: Jibril (AS) came to the Prophet {{1}} and asked a question.
blocks.51: Jibril came to the Prophet {{1}} and said, how do you count the fighters of Badr among you? He said, among the best of the Muslims, or some words like that. Jibril said, and so are the angels who were present at Badr.{{2}}
blocks.52: This rank stayed with them later too. A few years later a mistake of Hatib ibn Abi Balta‘ah (RA) was caught. He had secretly sent a letter to the polytheists of Makkah.
blocks.54: ‘Umar (RA) said again, he has betrayed Allah, His Messenger and the believers. Let me strike his neck. The Prophet {{1}} said, is he not one of the fighters of Badr? Perhaps Allah looked at the fighters of Badr and said, do what you wish, Paradise has become obligatory for you, or said, I have forgiven you. Tears came to ‘Umar’s (RA) eyes. He said, Allah and His Messenger know best.{{2}}
blocks.56: We measure a person by their latest mistake. The Prophet {{1}} measured also by sacrifice. Parents, teacher, friend, husband or wife, anyone, over one mistake we forget ten years of sacrifice.
blocks.58: After Badr, a different tune was heard from a group of the Jews of Madinah. The Prophet {{1}} gathered Banu Qaynuqa‘ in their market. He said, fear what has come upon Quraysh. Accept Islam. They said, Muhammad, do you think we are your people? Do not be deceived because you met people who do not know war. If you fight us, you will see what kind of people we are.{{2}}
blocks.59: Not long after, an incident in the market. A Muslim woman was sitting in the shop of a goldsmith of Qaynuqa‘. They wanted her to uncover her face. She did not agree. The goldsmith tied the corner of her garment to her back. When she stood up, her body was exposed, and they burst out laughing. A Muslim young man killed the goldsmith. The Jews killed that young man.{{1}}
blocks.60: The treaty was broken. The Prophet {{1}} besieged their fortress. Fifteen nights. In the end they were forced to come down, accepting his judgment. Then the hypocrite chief ‘Abdullah ibn Ubayy seized his coat of mail and said, treat my friends well. Will you cut them all down in a single morning? I fear misfortune. In the end the Prophet {{2}} said, they are yours. Another ally of theirs was ‘Ubadah ibn al-Samit (RA). He said, I am a friend of Allah, His Messenger and the believers. I free myself from the friendship of those disbelievers.{{3}}
blocks.61: Two allies of the same group. One said, I fear misfortune. The other said, I belong to Allah and the Messenger. We too, often out of fear of losing a job, fear of society, fear of losing a relationship, stand beside the wrong side.
blocks.62: Meanwhile Abu Sufyan had sworn not to pour water over his head until he had fought Muhammad. He came near Madinah with two hundred riders, killed an Ansari and his ally, and went back. The Prophet {{1}} pursued them. To lighten their load they threw away sacks of sawiq (roasted barley meal) and fled. Hence the name al-Sawiq, the Battle of the Barley Meal.{{2}}
blocks.63: Ka‘b ibn al-Ashraf was a Jewish chief. When he heard the news of Badr he said, if Muhammad has defeated these, then the belly of the earth is better than its back. He went to Makkah and incited Quraysh to war. Returning to Madinah, he began composing obscene verse naming Muslim women, and mocked the Prophet {{1}} and the Companions.{{2}}
blocks.66: Who is for Ka‘b ibn al-Ashraf? He has harmed Allah and His Messenger. Muhammad ibn Maslamah (RA) stood up. He said, O Messenger of Allah, do you want me to kill him? He said, yes.{{1}}
blocks.67: Muhammad ibn Maslamah (RA) hardly ate for three days. He said, O Messenger of Allah, I have given you a word; I do not know whether I will be able to keep it. The Prophet {{1}} said, upon you is only the effort. Some Ansar killed Ka‘b at night.{{2}}
blocks.68: Poetry was the mass media of that time. Today there are posts, memes, comments. It takes five seconds to type an insinuation about someone’s mother, sister or wife. This incident was by the order of the head of state, in a state of war, against a chief, in the context of treaty-breaking and incitement to war. It was not an instance of an individual taking the law into their own hands. What falls to our share is only to guard our own tongue and fingers.
blocks.70: From the spoils of Badr a she-camel had come to ‘Ali (RA) as his share. From the khumus the Prophet {{1}} had given him another.
blocks.72: On the day of Badr I had one she-camel as my share of the spoils. And that day the Prophet {{1}} gave me another from the khumus. When I wanted to set up home with Fatimah (RA), the daughter of the Prophet {{2}}, I arranged with a goldsmith of Banu Qaynuqa‘ that he would come with me to bring idhkhir grass. I thought I would sell it to the goldsmiths and raise the expense of the wedding feast.{{3}}
blocks.73: Cutting grass and selling it to cover the cost of a wedding feast. This was ‘Ali’s (RA) means. The Prophet {{1}} said, give her something.
blocks.75: When ‘Ali (RA) married Fatimah (RA), the Messenger of Allah {{1}} said to him, give her something. He said, I have nothing. He said, where is that Hutamiyyah coat of mail of yours?{{2}}
blocks.76: That coat of mail became the mahr.{{1}}
blocks.77: The Prophet {{1}} furnished Fatimah’s (RA) home: a cloth sheet, a water-skin, a leather pillow with idhkhir grass inside it.{{2}}
blocks.78: We go to excess in wedding expenses. The foundation on which a daughter’s home is built is not named decoration. It is honesty and love. After some time in the household, Fatimah (RA) felt the hardship of grinding at the hand-mill.
blocks.80: Fatimah (RA) complained of the hardship of grinding. She heard that some captives had come to the Messenger of Allah {{1}}. She went and asked for a servant, but did not find him. She mentioned it to ‘A’ishah (RA). When the Prophet {{2}} came, ‘A’ishah (RA) informed him. He came to us when we had already lain down. We went to get up. He said, stay as you are. I felt the coolness of his feet on my chest. He said, shall I teach you something better than what you asked for? When you go to bed, say Allahu Akbar thirty-four times, praise Allah thirty-three times, and recite tasbih thirty-three times. This is better for you than what you asked for.{{3}}
blocks.81: The one in the home who works hardest, do we see their hardship with our eyes? From whom do we get the news?
blocks.83: Some pictures remain from this dars of Badr. Three hundred and thirteen who set out to catch a caravan. Those who arrived at the field. A night when everyone slept and one person wept. A tent where, while making du‘a, the cloak slipped off, and someone lifted it back. A date, two teenage boys’ question, a promise. In the middle of war, small people’s big decisions.
blocks.84: A necklace, a piece of bread, the bedside of a sick wife. Several of the greatest honours of Badr were close to home. On the field of swords there are small signs of love, and it is those that keep a person human. The next dars is Uhud. There, the test that comes after this victory.
blocks.85: So take one task with you from today’s dars.
blocks.87: Seeing a necklace, the Prophet {{1}} had remembered Khadijah (RA), who had gone before, and even on that hard day of Badr, the shadow on one boy’s face and one uncle’s groaning did not escape his eyes and ears.
blocks.88: Today I will ask myself one question: the person in the home who toils silently for me every day, does that person know I have not forgotten them? Today I will make one person at home understand, by one word or one deed, that they have not been forgotten; something I will not give up from today on.

The Prophet’s ﷺ announcement about Ka‘b

quiz.q: What does the weeping of the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) after the ransom decision show?
o: Losing sleep over a loved one’s pain
Standing with the wrong side in the name of fear
Tears instead of excuses when a mistake is caught
Failing while keeping an oath made out of arrogance

quiz.q: What did Zaynab, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (RA), send along with her husband’s ransom?

A cloth sheet and a blanket
A necklace of her mother Khadijah (RA)

quiz.q: Among the behaviours in the story of ‘Abbas (RA), which is the behaviour of justice?
o: Losing sleep for the uncle on hearing his groaning
Not conceding even one dirham of the ransom
Arranging for the bonds to be loosened

quiz.q: Under Quraysh’s ban on weeping, what does the weeping over a lost camel point to?

Even household service is the reward of Badr
The consequence of speaking the truth
Putting loved ones first in a place of risk

You will not concede even one dirham

o: Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh (RA) and Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA)
Abu Jahl and al-Akhnas ibn Shariq
